questions.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{n}^{n/2}}{3{n}^{{n}^{2}}}.$ Does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{n}^{n/2}}{3{n}^{{n}^{2}}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{n}^{n/2}}{3{n}^{{n}^{2}}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt[n]{3}\cdot {n}^{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{\frac{1}{3}}\cdot \frac{1}{{n}^{n-1/2}} \\  & =1\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{\frac{1}{3}}=1.
$$

Since $L=0<1,$ the series converges by the root test.

questions.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{11}^{n}}{{7}^{n}\cdot n!}.$ Does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{11}^{n}}{{7}^{n}\cdot n!}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{11}^{n}}{{7}^{n}\cdot n!})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{11}{7\cdot \sqrt[n]{n!}}) \\  & =\frac{11}{7}{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{\frac{1}{n!}} \\  & =\frac{11}{7}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}

$$

questions.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}}.$ According to the root test, does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n+1}}{(9+5n)^{n}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{5}^{n}{n}^{n}\cdot n}{(9+5n)^{n}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{5n\sqrt[n]{n}}{9+5n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(\sqrt[n]{n}\cdot \frac{5n}{n})}{(\frac{9}{n}+\frac{5n}{n})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{5\sqrt[n]{n}}{(\frac{9}{n}+5)} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 1}{0+5} \\  & =\frac{5}{5} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{n}=1.
$$

Since $L=1,$ the root test gives no conclusion.

questions.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}}.$ According to the root test, does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{{6}^{n}}{{5}^{n}{n}^{6}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{6}{5\cdot \sqrt[n]{{n}^{6}}}) \\  & =\frac{6}{5}{lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{1}{\sqrt[n]{n}})}^{6} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\cdot {1}^{6} \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{n}=1.
$$

Since $L=\frac{6}{5}>1,$ the series diverges by the root test.

questions.problem: Calculate $L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ for the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{(10n)^{n}n}{(8n+1)^{n}}.$ According to the root test, does ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ converge or diverge?
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose we have the series ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}$ such that ${a}_{n}\ge 0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and that $L$ is defined as  

$$
L={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n}.
$$

 

Then, the root test states the following:

- If $L<1$, the series converges.

- If $L>1$ or $L=\infty $, the series diverges.

- If $L=1$, the root test is inconclusive.

We have the sequence ${a}_{n},$ defined as

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(10n)^{n}n}{(8n+1)^{n}}.
$$

To apply the root test, we find the limit of $\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}}$ as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{{a}_{n}} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{({a}_{n})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }{(\frac{(10n)^{n}n}{(8n+1)^{n}})}^{1/n} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }(\frac{10n\sqrt[n]{n}}{8n+1}) \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{10n\sqrt[n]{n}}{n(8+\frac{1}{n})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{10\sqrt[n]{n}}{(8+\frac{1}{n})} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 1}{8+0} \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we used the fact that

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }\sqrt[n]{n}=1.
$$

Since $L=\frac{5}{4}>1,$ the series diverges by the root test.
